value: The FAA's status summary stopped listing the nationwide ground stop at about 8:23 PM ET, but no lift has been announced; Advisory 120 ran through 11 PM ET and the next FAA planning call is 9:15 PM ET. No official cause; the FAA calls it a telecommunications outage.

Chicago was first in the FAA paperwork; whether the failure technically started there is still unclear. Public carrier status, user-report levels and internet routing data all look normal, which points to a failure inside the FAA's own leased network rather than a public carrier outage. CBS, citing multiple sources, reports that an update to the L3Harris-operated ATC network caused a reboot and crash. That report is sourced journalism, not an official confirmation, and it is not a confirmed cause.
